newsitem.title: NORWAY: DnB moves to take over BNbank.
newsitem.headline: DnB moves to take over BNbank.

text.p: Den norske Bank (DnB), Norway's largest bank, said on Wednesday it had won 82.5 percent acceptance for its bid to take over mortgage lender BNbank.

DnB said in a statement to the Oslo Bourse it planned to submit a formal application on Thursday to the Finance Ministry -- the regulatory body -- for permission to own between 82 and 100 percent of shares in BNbank.
The statement said the 82.5 percent included shares held by DnB, shares which DnB had an option to buy and pledges of acceptance from BNbank shareholders of its bid.
BNbank said last Friday its board had recommended to shareholders who had not responded to DnB's takeover offer to accept the bid as soon as possible.
DnB a week ago raised its offer by five crowns to 203.50 crowns per share excluding dividend.
The bank launched its bid in March in competition with a rival bid for BNbank by Fokus Bank.
Fokus, Norway's fourth biggest bank, has a share exchange offer valuing BNbank at 2.06 billion crowns.
Fokus Bank said last Friday it would not sell its 10 percent stake in BNbank to rival bidder DnB.
DnB spokesman Sigurd Ulven said DnB could either merge with BNbank or take it over, but that Fokus currently was blocking a takeover.
"Through the application to own between 82 and 100 percent we do not rule out any of the options," he told Reuters.
